sections.h2: How is Chandler laid out, and where does it sit in the Phoenix area?
sections.html:
Chandler is a Maricopa County city in the East Valley, about 22 miles southeast of downtown Phoenix, and it is the fourth most populous city in Arizona. The Census Bureau estimates 278,748 residents as of July 1, 2025. The city covers about 65.6 square miles.

Two freeways cut Chandler into three parts. Loop 202 (the Santan Freeway) and Loop 101 (the Price Freeway) divide the city into North, West and South Chandler, and Interstate 10 runs along the westernmost border. The San Tan Mountains lie on the Gila River Indian Community land nearby.

Where a house sits in those three areas changes what a buyer cares about. Homes near the Price Freeway put a buyer close to the city's large employers, while South Chandler houses are tied to the Loop 202 commute. Mention the freeway access and the nearest employment area when you describe your house.

sections.h2: What built Chandler's economy, and who are the big employers?
sections.html:
Chandler started as a ranch town and became one of the Valley's main technology centers. Dr. Alexander John Chandler, the first veterinary surgeon in Arizona Territory, settled south of Mesa in 1891 and had gathered 18,000 acres by 1900. The town-site office opened on May 16, 1912, and Maricopa County incorporated Chandler on February 16, 1920, after 186 residents petitioned for it.

Williams Air Force Base opened in 1941, yet Chandler still counted only 3,800 people in 1950. Growth sped up with chip and electronics plants from firms such as Microchip, Motorola and Intel, and the city passed 30,000 residents by 1980.

The city's Price Corridor, 5.7 square miles around the Loop 101 and Loop 202 interchange, holds 783 businesses and 41,620 jobs. The city lists these notable employers there:

  • Intel, 10,000 employees
  • Wells Fargo, 5,500
  • Bank of America, 3,600
  • Northrop Grumman, 1,700
  • Microchip Technology, 1,700

Two hospitals add to local employment: Chandler Regional Medical Center and Banner Ocotillo Medical Center. For a seller, the practical point is that many Chandler buyers relocate for these jobs, and they often need to close on a set schedule.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Chandler homes and households?
sections.html:
Chandler has the highest home values of the four Arizona cities in the Census comparison used for this guide, with a median owner-occupied value of $507,800. The table shows the 2020 to 2024 QuickFacts figures.

About 86.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most neighborhoods are stable and a house for sale is often compared with a few recent sales on the same street. The population changed by only 1.0% between the April 2020 base and July 2025, which points to a built-out city.

sections.h2: Which school districts and campuses serve Chandler houses?
sections.html:
Several districts overlap in Chandler, so the district for your address depends on the street. Chandler Unified School District, Kyrene School District, Tempe Union High School District, Mesa Public Schools and Gilbert Public Schools all serve parts of the city. Catholic and charter options include Basis Schools and Seton Catholic Preparatory.

Chandler-Gilbert Community College serves about 13,000 students, and the University of Arizona has a Chandler location. When you list, name the exact district and school zone for your address, since buyers search by them.

sections.h2: Do I need permits for past work before selling a Chandler house?
sections.html:
Yes, any past work that needed a permit should have one, and the city warns that missing permits surface at sale time. Chandler's Development Services homeowner manual says unpermitted work can bring a Legal Notice or an Order to Comply and doubled permit fees. The city can order non-compliant work, such as a room addition, removed at the owner's cost, and FHA will not lend when county assessor records do not match the home.

The manual lists work that does not need a permit, including:

  • One-story detached accessory structures up to 120 square feet and 7 feet high
  • Fences not over 7 feet high
  • Retaining walls not over 4 feet high, unless they support a surcharge

You can view a home's permit history by entering the address at the city's online development permits portal. Questions go to the Plan Reviewer of the Day at 480-782-3078 or prod@chandleraz.gov. Homes in an HOA subdivision should also have HOA approval for projects, because the city does not enforce HOA rules.

sections.h2: What are Chandler's rules for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Chandler requires a city short-term rental license for each rental location, and the rules sit in Chapter 22 of the Chandler City Code. The city counts any property rented, advertised or offered on a web-based platform as a short-term rental, whatever the length of stay.

An owner must get an Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license, register the property as a rental with Maricopa County, notify neighbors, apply for the city license, post emergency contact information inside the unit and show the state and city license numbers in advertisements. The license runs to June 30 each year, and approval normally takes seven business days. Operating without a license can draw a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per month if the owner does not apply within 30 days of a written notice.

The city lists a combined short-term rental tax rate of 11.67%, made up of 4.40% Chandler and 7.27% state. If you are selling a house that has been a rental, the new owner will need to apply for their own license, so tell your buyer what the city requires.

sections.h2: How do recording, the affidavit and property tax work for a Chandler sale?
sections.html:
A Chandler deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder, whose standard fee is $30 per document. A deed needs either an affidavit of property value or an exemption code to be accepted, and the Recorder's Office says it cannot advise on which code fits. The office at 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200, Phoenix, is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and recorded originals mailed in come back within two to four weeks.

A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the affidavit to state the price, date, legal description and parcel number, and A.R.S. 11-1134 lists the exempt transfers. Escrow normally files these papers for you.

Arizona sets property tax due dates at October 1 and March 1, with delinquency after the next November 1 and May 1. The Maricopa County Treasurer's calendar shows 2026 first-half taxes became delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 2, 2026, so that deadline has passed. If a rental registration is on file, the Maricopa County Assessor shows the parcel type as Residential/Rental, so check it before you list.

faqs.q: How many people live in Chandler?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 278,748 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 275,987 counted in the 2020 census. Chandler is the fourth most populous city in Arizona.

faqs.q: Does Chandler require a permit for a room addition?
faqs.a: Yes. Chandler's homeowner permit manual treats room additions and remodeling as permit work unless the item is on the exempt list. Check with the Plan Reviewer of the Day at 480-782-3078 before you start or if you are unsure about work a previous owner did.

faqs.q: What is the Maricopa County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $30 per document. The deed must also carry an affidavit of property value or an exemption code.

faqs.q: Who are the largest employers in Chandler?
faqs.a: The city lists Intel at 10,000 employees in the Price Corridor, followed by Wells Fargo at 5,500, Bank of America at 3,600, and Northrop Grumman and Microchip Technology at 1,700 each.

faqs.q: When did the first half of 2026 property tax become delinquent in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: First-half 2026 taxes became delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 2, 2026. Full-year taxes can be paid through December 31 without interest.
